intended_object: The canonical isomorphism of abelian groups H^n_cts(G, X restricted to ℤ) ≅ H^n_cts(G, X). It says that the continuous cohomology of a topological k-representation X of a topological group G, viewed only as a representation over ℤ, is the underlying abelian group of the continuous cohomology of X. This reading comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition takes `restrictScalarsIntIso` and turns it into an additive equivalence. That isomorphism is built in two steps:
1. The cochain-level isomorphism `homogeneousCochainsRestrictScalarsIntIso` gives an isomorphism on cohomology via `homologyMapIso`.
2. `mapHomologyIso` says that the exact restriction-of-scalars functor `TopModuleCat.restrictScalarsInt` commutes with homology.

This is the standard canonical identification: continuous cochains, their differentials, cocycles and coboundaries do not depend on the scalar ring. So H^n of the ℤ-restricted representation is H^n(G, X) as an abelian group. The companion lemma `π_comp_restrictScalarsIntIso_hom` confirms that the map sends the class of a cocycle to the class of the same cocycle, so this is the canonical map and not just some isomorphism.

On generality: the base k is any topological ring and G is any topological group, which is the natural setting. Mathlib has no counterpart for this continuous-cohomology comparison map. The isomorphism is a genuine canonical identification rather than an implementation artifact, and it is defined correctly.
